subject: Exception conditions
notes: cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.3 "If the executed statement is a MERGE or SORT statement, then the rules for those statements apply" -> OK 2). The population the adjudicator found unverifiable now exists and is disposed of by the verb (kb/Work PB1036): CobolSort marks every fatal condition its SORT/MERGE statement entries raise (Init, FileNotOpen, the implicit Release, Sort, Merge - an exception FILTER that sets CobolFatalException.RaisedBySortMerge and declines the catch), and the SORT/MERGE statement guard (EcEmitter.VerbDisposes) runs the declarative and then terminates the statement instead of re-throwing, for a marked condition only. The rule keys on the statement that EXECUTED, so the mark - not the exception-name - decides: an EC-LOCALE-* raised by a locale-collated key during the sequence phase is marked (the filter wraps Sort/Merge; not separately witnessed), while the same EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE raised by a RELEASE statement, or anything raised by a statement of a procedure range, stays unmarked and keeps 5)/7) (unit TheStatementsOwnRaise_IsMarked_TheReleaseStatementsIsNot). Golden cases A, B, C, E, G: the D-V declarative completes NORMALLY and control still returns after the statement. The EC-I-O half is reachable at last: EcBinder.QueryFor asks the EC-I-O family per USING/GIVING file, arming the __IoCheckEc(__verbRule: true) hooks that had a zero mask before (golden case H: IO=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR, then H US=35). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 D-SMA (b). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/EcBinder.cs#QueryFor (EcWrap's QueryFor closure is replaced by the one enumeration DeclaredRaisableNames (kb/Work PB3102))
